evals.name: relay-web-focus-mode
evals.prompt: Make a ~20s cinematic promo reel of Relay's Focus mode: in Settings you turn it on and the inbox then only shows your team's issues. The app is in evals/fixtures/relay-web (React). Our users are on Linux and Windows laptops. Remotion is not installed: create the reel as its own package and install exact-pinned remotion and @remotion/* versions with npm. Put the deliverables in outputs/: reel.mp4, storyboard.md and the frames you reviewed.
evals.expected_output: A 15 to 30s 1920x1080 reel rendered from Relay's real components, showing the inbox before and after Focus mode, with a storyboard whose easings match the code and all three gate scripts passing.
assertions: outputs/reel.mp4 exists, is 1920x1080 and lasts between 15 and 30 seconds (ffprobe)
The video opens from black and ends on a fade to black (first and last frames are near black)

The title card's headline holds for its reading time: visible characters / 17 + 0.5s (minimum 0.8s), measured from the moment the whole headline has fully settled (last word's reveal finished) to the start of its exit
The product's entrance starts before the title's exit has finished (overlap, no empty frames between them, checked on frames around the handoff)

Every caption, keycap and piece of on-screen explanatory text holds for its reading time under the same fully-settled rule, with chapter numbers and keycap labels counted, lines joined by single spaces and a 0.8s minimum

The storyboard names an easing (a cubic-bezier, spring config or named curve) for every animated element, including captions, keycaps, cursor, highlights, ambient drift and the fades, not only verbs like rises or slides

The storyboard lists the determinism risks found in this product and how each is neutralised (CSS transitions or animation classes, clocks, randomness, timers, async effects, network fonts or data), or states that each was checked and absent
The camera does not ease to a stop at intermediate keyframes: the code interpolates through keys (for example a monotone cubic) with stops only at intended holds
The reel renders the product's real UI (imports the real components, or uses strings and layout taken from the real CLI source) and flags any invented data as placeholder
Rendered frames were reviewed and the review is written down: stills or contact sheets are saved in outputs/ together with a log of what they showed and what changed

On frames extracted in the middle of each caption and each push-in, captions and keycaps do not overlap product content (blurred product content counts) or each other and no text line, row or control is sliced at the frame edge (window chrome bleeding cleanly off the frame is allowed)
Fonts come from the product, the repo, a licensed package or the product's own CDN font family, not files copied from the system font folder or another application
Window chrome and keyboard labels target Linux and Windows users (no macOS traffic lights, no ⌘ glyphs)

The storyboard's easing inventory matches the code: each easing it names is the one the code applies to that element (helper defaults included, for example a tween with no easing argument is not linear) and no animated element in the code is missing from it

No window or card border rests within 3.5% of the frame edge (67px left or right, 38px top or bottom) for 0.6s or more: borders stay inside that margin or bleed clearly off the frame (`edge-scan.mjs <reel> --json` lists no TIGHT range, confirmed on frames)
In every handoff that brings in text (title, captions, end card) the text never appears over product content that is still visible, sharp or blurred, checked on frames at the midpoint of each handoff

The deliverables present no known problem as acceptable: every crop, collision, over-length, short hold or edge issue the run's own log, storyboard or report mentions is fixed in the final render or shown not to be a problem by a stated rule, not left as accepted, known or for later
Every handoff overlaps, product to end card included: no frame between the product leaving and the end card or a caption arriving is empty or near-empty (checked on frames at each handoff)
Every UI element on screen exists in the product as it ships: nothing the product hides or disables is drawn as real, and anything drawn for the reel is flagged as a placeholder

Any problem the run rules 'not a problem' cites a rule that covers it and a premise that holds in the product's own code (a claim about how a library renders is traced through the code path that runs)
Features and captions use Relay's own names for things (Inbox, Focus mode, Quick find, as in its UI copy and README), not invented labels
The reel shows the inbox both before and after Focus mode is turned on, so the effect of the setting is visible

The storyboard lists this product's determinism risks: the clock-based greeting, the CSS transition and keyframe classes (.card, .dialog) and the 120ms debounced search, each with how it is neutralised

evals.name: review-flawed-reel
evals.prompt: Can you review our status page promo reel before we do the final render? The project is in evals/fixtures/flawed-reel. Write your review to review.md.
evals.expected_output: A severity-ranked review that finds the seeded flaws in the fixture.
assertions: Flags the Command palette caption held about 1.2s as far below its reading time
Flags the gap between the title leaving (about 2.6s) and the product entering (3.2s) as an empty or queued handoff
Flags the 27s arrow-key walk at 0.08s steps as both too long and too fast to follow, and the 41s total as too long
Flags the end card as too short and ending in a hard cut with no fade
Flags the camera as stop-go: interpolate with ease-in-out across many keyframes stops at every key
Flags the product entrance using an ease-in curve on an arrival
Flags Math.random in the star field as non-deterministic across frames
Flags the new Date() time-of-day greeting as non-deterministic
Flags the transition and animate-pulse utility classes as unkilled CSS animation
Flags the Google Fonts stylesheet link as a network fetch at render time
Flags the caption bottom-left colliding with the product framed left at high zoom
Flags the page change at 8.1s happening while the camera is zoomed in elsewhere
Flags the dashboard as a recreated mock instead of real components and the uptime and recovery numbers as invented unflagged data
Flags that storyboard.md says the Command palette caption comes in with emphasized decelerate while Captions.tsx interpolates its opacity linearly, a storyboard easing that does not match the code
Flags the dashboard's right border at about x 1910 (left 320 plus width 1590), about 10px from the frame edge and inside the action-safe margin
Flags the end card text drawn over the dashboard, which is still fully visible when the end card appears
Flags the README's accepted known issue (a table row cut by the frame edge during the push-in) as a problem to fix before the final render, not an acceptable caveat
Flags the 'Press ⌘K to search' hint as unverified against the real product (nothing in the project backs it up) and as a macOS glyph
Findings are severity ranked with file and line or cue references and each has a concrete fix
